# Decision Log

Record every non-trivial decision made during the build: what, why, alternatives
considered. Append-only.

| # | Phase | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | Money = integer cents, branded type; round-half-away-from-zero | Auditability; floats forbidden by spec |
| 2 | 0 | Business dates are date-only (YYYY-MM-DD), single dates.ts utility | Timezone bugs are the top fintech date hazard |
| 3 | 0 | Obligation timeline computed on demand, not stored | Single source of truth; avoids cache-invalidation bugs |
| 4 | 0 | Weekend/holiday due dates adjust to PRIOR business day (conservative) | Funds present early is safe; late is not |
| 5 | 0 | v1 minimum-path interest = simple monthly (carried × APR/12), labeled approximate **[SUPERSEDED by #29: now average-daily-balance]** | Hand-verifiable; ADB method is roadmap |
| 6 | 1 | SQLite for local dev/test via Prisma 7 (`prisma-client` generator → `src/generated/prisma`); schema kept Postgres-portable (no SQLite-only features; enums/Json represented as String columns with documented values) | Postgres unavailable in build env; CLAUDE.md explicitly allows SQLite |
| 7 | 1 | Business dates stored as String `YYYY-MM-DD` (not DateTime @db.Date) | SQLite has no DATE type; lexicographic compare works; single dates.ts utility validates |
| 8 | 1 | Added `BalanceSnapshot` model (month-end balance per account) | Drives the net-worth trend chart deterministically from seeded history; additive over the Phase 0 draft shape |
| 9 | 1 | "This cycle" = obligations from GENERATED statements; a not-yet-generated statement (estimate) is next cycle — shown as upcoming, excluded from headline/projection — unless no generated statement exists at all (then the estimate IS the answer) | An un-generated statement closes in the future and is due even later, so it can never bind before current statements; keeps the headline answer and its hand math stable |
| 10 | 1 | Within a projected day: scheduled flows post BEFORE card payments are drawn | ACH credits typically post before card-payment cutoffs; deterministic, tested, surfaced in assumptions |
| 11 | 1 | Seed's engineered intra-period dip placed between the two due dates (rent 06-24, payroll 06-26): endpoints positive, mid-period −$1,012.33 | With checking ≈$3,400 and total due $5,412.33 fixed by SEED_SPEC, a pre-06-15 below-zero dip that fully recovers is arithmetically impossible; this placement is the exact mirror of edge case H (endpoint fine, intra-period negative) |
| 12 | 1 | Demo mode pins "today" via `DEMO_TODAY` env (default = seed asOf 2026-06-10) | Engines take `today` as input; keeps the seeded dataset coherent and e2e deterministic |
| 13 | 1 | Phase 1 auth = Auth.js v5 Credentials "demo sign-in" (one click, demo user only); magic-link/Google land in Phase 4 with the security pass | Demo mode must work with zero secrets; full auth is a Phase 4 acceptance item |
| 14 | 1 | Seed statement history balances are plausible PRNG values, not exact sums of that cycle's card transactions | Reconciliation adds heavy complexity with no Phase 1–3 test value; noted as a known limitation in STATUS |
| 15 | 1 | Transfer recommendation byDate clamped to `today` (critic P1-1) | "Transfer by yesterday" is an impossible instruction; same-day transfer is the correct remedy |
| 16 | 1 | Current statement = most recent with dueDate ≥ today OR an unpaid remainder (critic P1-2) | A delinquent statement is real debt due NOW, never a next-cycle estimate |
| 17 | 2 | Mid-band amounts on a merchant with user amount-banded rules go to review | The user declared the merchant context-dependent; the gap between bands is genuinely ambiguous (EDGE_CASES §Categorization) |
| 18 | 2 | "Possibly unused" subscription heuristic = fitness-category memberships (usage is not observable in transaction data) | Surfaced as a question to the user, never an accusation; consistent with coach guardrails |
| 19 | R1 | Cash-needed engine `notes`/`assumptions` ARE presentation strings (formatCents/formatISODate inside the engine) — a deliberate exemption from the "format only at the UI boundary" convention, same as coach-copy.ts | The engine's auditability story requires self-describing output; structured note objects are a localization-era refactor |
| 20 | R1 | TanStack Query (named in CLAUDE.md conventions) is intentionally NOT used | Server components + server actions made client-side query caching unnecessary; zero client data-fetching exists |
| 21 | R1 | v1 minimum-path interest remains simple-monthly; PHASE_0 §4's "binding" ADB wording is superseded by DECISIONS #5 **[now itself superseded by #29 — ADB implemented, matching PHASE_0 §4's original intent]** | The in-app label, STATUS #2 and ROADMAP #3 all agree; PHASE_0 annotated in place |
| 22 | R2 | Required ingestion pipeline order for ANY future transaction source (Plaid, CSV, manual): normalizeMerchant → merchant upsert → loadUserRules → categorize(rules) → persist category/confidence/needsReview → detectTransfers → detectRecurring → ScheduledTransaction refresh | Without this single documented order, every new source re-creates the severed-rules-loop bug (review cycle 1, C2); ROADMAP #1 references it |
| 23 | R2 | Batch "apply to all" scopes to the EXACT raw descriptor for aggregate pseudo-merchants (Zelle/checks), to the merchant otherwise; aggregate rules are also dropped at the rule READ path | "All 6 payments to J. Park" is a sane batch; "all Zelle ever" is not (review cycle 2) |
| 24 | R4 | A manually-entered transaction records ACTIVITY only — it does NOT mutate the owning account's `currentBalanceCents` | Balances are provider-authoritative (the institution/seed is the source of truth); rewriting one from a freeform entry would desync the reconciled snapshot AND perturb the cash-needed engine + the pinned golden net-worth/headline values. A dedicated derived-balance "Cash" account is the clean future path (ROADMAP). The entry still flows into all transaction-based views (register, spending, insights) |
| 25 | R4 | Manual entry runs the categorize() arm of the #22 pipeline (normalizeMerchant → loadUserRules → categorize → persist category/confidence/needsReview, with isTransfer set from the verdict/explicit category) but intentionally skips merchant-table upsert and recurring re-detection | A single user-entered row has no cadence to detect, and the register's display name already falls back to the cleaned descriptor when no Merchant row exists — so the skipped steps add cost without changing behavior for one row. Full #22 order still binds for bulk sources (Plaid/CSV) |
| 26 | R4 | Plaid integration split into a TESTED pure mapping layer (plaid-map.ts: sign flip, account-type, liability→statement, per-row categorize) and an UNVERIFIED network layer (plaid.ts). Access tokens + sync cursor live in a dedicated `PlaidItem` table, not packed into Account.providerRef | The mapping is where silent ledger-corrupting bugs hide (sign flips, float→cents, liability classification) so it must be unit-tested even though live calls can't be in this env; the network layer is honestly labeled UNVERIFIED rather than claimed working. `PlaidItem` is the clean store ROADMAP #1 called for. Plaid amounts are floats — plaid-map is the single boundary where a float becomes cents (rounded once), preserving the no-float-money rule everywhere downstream |
| 27 | R4 | CSV import is the third ingest source (DECISIONS #22), fully testable without credentials. Contract: required `date`/`description`/`amount` (+ optional `category`) headers with aliases; amount SIGNED in Pulse convention (negative = out); dates as ISO or US MM/DD/YYYY; malformed rows skipped with per-line errors, good rows still imported. Like manual entry it records activity only, never mutates balances (#24) | A real user can get real transactions in TODAY by exporting a bank CSV — no Plaid, no keys — which is the highest-value go-live step that is verifiable in this environment. Signed-amount + explicit date formats avoid the ambiguity that breaks Mint/Simplifi imports; per-row error reporting means one bad line never silently drops a whole file |
| 29 | R5 | Minimum-path interest upgraded from the labeled simple-monthly approximation (carried × APR/12) to the **average-daily-balance method** (ROADMAP #3, supersedes #5/#21). Per card not paid in full: interest = round(DPR × Σ daily balances) over the next cycle [close → close+1mo], DPR = APR/10000/365, balance = full statement until the minimum posts on the due date then the carried balance after; grace-gated (paid in full → $0); new purchases not projected. Pure primitive `averageDailyBalanceInterestCents` in money.ts (own known-answer tests); the engine derives cycleDays/daysUntilDue from the statement's close+due dates (estimate path uses nextCycleClose/nextDue). Every pinned value recomputed by hand and updated with its test (EDGE_CASES §I; seed $65.76→$67.36, §I $59.30→$61.08, critic5 §I $58.81, S8 $12.23, N6 $19.17/$18.74) | The v1 formula was always labeled a documented approximation awaiting ADB (#5/#21, STATUS #2). ADB is the method real issuers use and the constitution's "financial math is sacred" priority; it is hand-verifiable and e2e-verifiable. The value is cycle-date dependent (two §I anchors differ), which is correct — the doc and tests now pin both. Grace-gating preserves the autopay-in-full = $0 behavior the old `carried` formula gave for free; modeling interest on the full balance until the minimum posts captures the lost-grace reality the flat formula missed |
| 28 | R5 | Money Dials settings/onboarding UI (`/settings`) edits the five per-user dials the engines already read but nothing could set: payment account, SWR, expected return, hourly wage, money dials. Validation lives in a pure engine module (`engine/settings/dials.ts`, 80 unit cases) — string-only parse, all-fields-at-once errors, bounds chosen so the FI engine stays defined (SWR rejected ≤ 0 because `fiNumberCents` divides by it; SWR ≤ 10%, return 0–15%, wage ≤ $10k/hr). The e2e mutates ONLY `moneyDials` (the one dial coupled to no golden value) and restores it; numeric dials are only ever written back at seed values, so the pinned cash-needed/FI numbers are never perturbed under the fullyParallel shared-DB e2e. Payment account is restricted to owned CHECKING/SAVINGS (you fund card payments from cash). Onboarding nudge on the dashboard is gated on `paymentAccountId == null` → dormant in demo (zero DOM change for existing e2e), and activates for real new users once auth/signup lands | These dials were hardcoded in the seed with no way for a real user to change them — the credential-free half of ROADMAP #2. Engine-first (per CLAUDE.md) means the risky part (parse/bounds/normalize) is exhaustively unit-tested in isolation; the server action is a thin ownership-scoped persist + audit. Gating onboarding on the payment account (the single input the whole cash-needed answer is built on) is both the semantically correct "you're not set up yet" signal and the choice that keeps the demo dashboard byte-identical for the golden above-the-fold e2e |

Pure engine `engine/budgets/status.ts` (`summarizeBudgets` over the union of spent+target categories with over/remaining/pct; `netSpendByCategory` nets refunds; `isBudgetable`/`parseBudgetTargetCents`). `setBudget` is an atomic `prisma.budget.upsert` on a new `@@unique([userId, categoryId])`; `clearBudget` is an ownership-scoped deleteMany; both audit-logged. Budget targets are DISPLAY-ONLY — they feed nothing but the /budgets view (not cash-needed/FI/net-worth), so writes perturb no golden value. **Budgets net refunds locally** (signed-sum per category, keep net-outflow) even though app-wide refund-netting is deferred (ROADMAP #4 / STATUS #9): this is the FIRST surface to turn category spend into an over/under verdict + colored bar, so a gross number would mislabel a net-under-target category "over" | Found by the budget Hostile Critic (two P1s, both fixed): (1) refund-blindness would fire a false "over target" amber bar — fixed by netting within the budgets spend calc (scoped to display; the income/savings-rate aggregations stay gross per the documented convention); (2) the overwrite path was untested with no DB uniqueness guard — fixed with `@@unique` + `upsert` (structurally one row, no race) plus an e2e overwrite step. Category picker + server validation share one `isBudgetable` allow-list so the accepted set equals the offered set (no off-menu income/transfer targets). Throwing on invalid input matches the sibling `createGoal` |
| 31 | R5 | Account deletion / "delete my data" UI (ROADMAP #10, PRIVACY.md §Deletion). Typed-confirmation gate (`confirmationMatches`, pure-tested) → ownership-scoped `prisma.user.delete` that cascades every user-owned row (`onDelete: Cascade` on all relations; shared Merchant/Category left intact) → best-effort Plaid token-revoke first → `signOut`. The action is IDEMPOTENT: an existence guard skips the audit+delete when the row is already gone (double-submit / stale session / unseeded deploy) and still signs out, instead of an unhandled FK(P2003)/not-found(P2025) 500. A live deletion summary shows the high-signal counts + an honest catch-all for derived history. The destructive EXECUTION is verified by an integration test that calls the real action against throwaway users (gate-reject → no deletion; exact phrase → scoped wipe + signOut; idempotent re-run) — NOT e2e'd against the shared demo user (would break the fullyParallel suite); the e2e covers the gate + summary only. Added `(app)/error.tsx` so a post-deletion no-accounts render (or any action throw) degrades to a recoverable screen, not a raw 500 | Found/hardened by the deletion Hostile Critic (4 P1s, all fixed; cascade correctness verified down to live PRAGMA foreign_keys): the cascade was correct but (1) the action had zero execution coverage, (2) it crashed non-idempotently on an absent row, (3) post-deletion demo re-sign-in 500'd with no error boundary. Deletion is genuinely exposed now (the typed gate is the accident-safety, replacing the prior "Phase-5-deferred" stance); demo data is reseedable via `npx prisma db seed`. Multi-device session invalidation (JWT strategy) + a non-cascading compliance deletion-record are noted for the real-auth release (STATUS) |
| 32 | R5 | Offline PWA service worker (ROADMAP #5): `public/sw.js` + a precached `/offline` shell + production-only registration (`sw-register.tsx`). Deliberately minimal/conservative: navigations are NETWORK-FIRST (online always fresh, navigation responses NEVER cached → no stale/cross-user data online or on a shared device; offline → precached `/offline`); a tiny fixed icon/manifest allowlist is cache-first with a `res.ok` guard; hashed `/_next/static/*` is PASSTHROUGH (immutable + content-addressed → left to the browser HTTP cache, so SW storage stays bounded — no per-deploy accumulation). Precache is per-asset (`Promise.allSettled`) so one 404 can't void the shell; the `/offline` page is inline-styled (self-contained offline). Middleware excludes `/sw.js` (must serve as JS) and `/offline` (public shell), anchored (`offline$`/`sw\.js$`) so prefix collisions can't skip auth. `/sw.js` registered → scope `/` | Found/shaped by the PWA Hostile Critic (the 3 review-phase "P1"s — fixed cache name / atomic-precache-swallow / cache-first-stale-offline — were all adversarially downgraded to P2: no online stale-serving, no leak, no suite destabilization, verified to live PRAGMA-equivalent checks). The conservative design (network-first nav, passthrough hashed assets) is what keeps it from the classic SW footguns; the critic-flagged P2s were fixed proactively (res.ok guard, resilient precache, network-first /offline, self-contained shell, anchored matcher). A build-stamped cache name + an in-app update affordance are deferred (documented) — not needed while hashed assets are passthrough and online is network-first |

Backward-compatible — callers that don't pass `categoryId` are unchanged (positives stay income). 4 known-answer fixture tests; the demo provider returns `categoryId` so it's active in-app | The savings-rate/FI numbers should reflect what you actually spent, not gross-spend-plus-phantom-income when you return something. | 34 | R5 | Recurring detection is refund-robust (ROADMAP #4 tail, fixes STATUS #7's "refund+rebill drops the series"): `detectRecurring` now analyzes only the DOMINANT sign within each merchant group — a stray opposite-sign txn (a refund inside an expense subscription) is a one-off, excluded from cadence/amount analysis. Focused self-review + green suite, proportionate to the contained engine change |
| 35 | R5 | Postgres deploy path (ROADMAP, "engine before UI" extended to infra): the app runs on **SQLite locally + in every test** (zero credentials, `file:./dev.db`) and on **Postgres in production**, chosen at runtime by connection-string scheme in `src/lib/db-adapter.ts` (`isPostgresUrl` → `PrismaPg` else `PrismaBetterSqlite3`). ONE canonical schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`, provider sqlite); `scripts/gen-pg-schema.mjs` deterministically derives `prisma/.generated.postgres.prisma` (pure `provider` swap — the schema is already PG-portable: Int cents, String dates, no enum/Json/Decimal) so there is no second hand-maintained schema to drift. `prisma.config.ts` `schema` is env-driven (`PRISMA_SCHEMA ?? canonical`); `vercel.json` `buildCommand` = derive → `prisma generate` → `prisma db push` → `next build`. Drivers kept out of the server bundle via `serverExternalPackages`. Deployed DB = a dedicated `pulse` database on the user's existing Neon instance (separate from VitaForge's `neondb`, created with `CREATE DATABASE`; VitaForge untouched). Runtime URL is the Neon **direct (non-pooled) endpoint**, not the `-pooler` one. Required Vercel env: `DATABASE_URL` (pulse direct), `AUTH_SECRET`. Pure unit test on the scheme detector + adapter type (`tests/unit/db-adapter.test.ts`); the Postgres path was provisioned + seeded for real (842 txns, 9 accounts, 11 series) as proof, not assumed | A stateful app cannot run on Vercel's read-only/ephemeral serverless FS with a bundled SQLite file — the deferred "needs Postgres" step. Adapter-by-URL keeps the demo-mode invariant (local/tests stay credential-free SQLite) while production gets real Postgres, with the generated client's provider matched to the runtime adapter (Prisma validates this). The **direct endpoint** is deliberate: Neon's pooled endpoint is PgBouncer in transaction mode, which breaks node-postgres prepared statements (`@prisma/adapter-pg`); for a low-traffic demo the direct endpoint's lower connection ceiling is a non-issue, and switching to `@prisma/adapter-neon` (WebSocket pooling) is the documented path if scale ever needs the pooler. Reusing VitaForge's `neondb` was rejected outright — overlapping table names (`User`) mean `prisma db push` would alter/clobber the other project; a separate database is free and fully isolated |
| 36 | R5 | Inline recategorization on the transaction register (user request). The pipeline auto-files transactions and routes only low-confidence ones (`needsReview`) to the triage inbox — so a CONFIDENT-but-wrong guess was uncorrectable from the register (read-only category). Now every register row's category is a tappable editor (`category-editor.tsx`): pick a new category, then **"Just this once"** (single reversible Correction, no rule) or **"Always · all <merchant>"** (re-files EVERY transaction of that merchant — already-filed ones included — and creates a durable priority-100 CategorizationRule, so past + future are fixed in one action). Reuses the existing triage machinery: single path calls `applyCategory`; merchant path mirrors `applyToAllSimilar` + rule creation. Generalized `similarTransactionsWhere` with `onlyNeedsReview` (default true → triage unchanged; register passes false to reach already-filed rows) — ONE shared scope so the two surfaces can't drift (#23). "Always" is gated to real merchants with a known merchantId (never Zelle/checks aggregates). Pure helpers `ASSIGNABLE_CATEGORIES` + `isRuleEligibleMerchant` (`engine/categorize/assign.ts`) with known-answer tests; the destructive action is proven by an integration test driving the REAL action against throwaway users (scope 'one' = single + no rule; scope 'merchant' = all 3 incl. needsReview=false + priority-100 rule + ownership isolation); e2e recategorizes an isolated manual row (golden-safe per #24). This is the user-facing half of "AI learns categorization": corrections→rules is the existing supervised loop; surfacing it on the register is what makes confident misclassifications fixable. LLM-assist + accuracy/Brier surfacing (options B/C) deferred — not built | The register being read-only for categories meant the single most important correction path (fixing a wrong high-confidence guess) had no UI; triage only ever shows the <5% the pipeline already doubts. Reusing `applyCategory`/`applyToAllSimilar` (not a parallel mutation path) keeps the correction/rule/undo invariants intact — the same Correction rows, the same priority-100 rules the engine already honors, all reversible from triage. Engine-first per CLAUDE.md: the risky parts (assignable set, rule-eligibility, the generalized scope) are unit/integration-tested in isolation; the UI is thin wiring. Scoped to A (toggle only) per the user's explicit choice |
| 37 | R5 | Categorization accuracy + calibration metric (user request, option B; CLAUDE.md §adaptive-runtime "log every prediction, track Brier, surface in UI"). New `CategoryPrediction` table logs one row per transaction — predictedCategoryId + confidenceBps, plus actualCategoryId (null until ground truth known). Pure engine `engine/accuracy/score.ts`: `scorePredictions` → {n, correct, accuracyBps, brierMilli}; Brier = mean((confidence/10000 − hit)²)×1000, so it scores CALIBRATION (a confident miss is punished harder than an unsure one), not just hit-rate. Known-answer tested (hand-verified 2/3 correct → Brier 0.300). Seeded: every transaction gets a prediction; actual is set only where genuinely known (a known merchant's canonical category), so the demo shows an honest measured number (~high, since known-merchant hits score well and low-confidence review items count as not-yet-correct with low confidence = good calibration); unknown/ambiguous rows stay unlabeled until reviewed. Ground truth accrues live: applyCategory / applyToAllSimilar / recategorize set actualCategoryId when the user confirms or corrects. Surfaced as an AccuracyCard on /triage (accuracy % + Brier + N, or a "no data yet" state). Integration-tested (recategorize labels the prediction; getCategorizationAccuracy reflects it) + e2e (card shows a %). Predictions cascade-delete with the user. NOT logged for manual/CSV ingest (user-/import-dictated categories aren't model predictions) — documented gap, those rows just aren't scored | "Improves over time" must be measurable, not asserted — this is the instrument. A separate log table (not derived from Corrections) avoids the conflation where a triage-accept and an AI-miss both look like "corrections"; predicted/confidence are frozen at predict-time and actual arrives later, which is exactly what a Brier score needs. Seeding actual only for known merchants keeps it honest (no fabricated ground truth for genuinely ambiguous rows). Brier×1000 as an int keeps the money/no-float discipline at the display boundary; the metric itself is a ratio so fractions are inherent and formatted at the UI |

Pure pieces (`engine/categorize/llm.ts`): `parseLlmCategory` validates the model's JSON against the known category set (our schema — unknown id / bad confidence / non-object → null), `buildCategorizePrompt`, and `pickAssistedCategory` — the LLM may override ONLY when the deterministic result was unsure (review/uncategorized) AND the model is confident (≥ AUTO_FLAGGED 7000bps); a confident deterministic call (known merchant, user rule) is never overridden. Server `suggestCategoryViaLLM` (Anthropic Messages API, model via env, default haiku): no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → returns null WITHOUT a network call; any network/parse/validation failure → null; never throws. | 90 | R5 | iOS safe-area inset for the fixed mobile bottom tab bar (closes the item #86 reverted after 3 e2e failures). FIRST measured the assumption: a throwaway Playwright probe (Pixel 5 + 380px, the e2e device) showed `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` resolves to **0px** in the emulator (CSS.supports=true, the 77px fallback did not apply) — so #86's "nonzero emulator inset grew the bar" diagnosis was WRONG; valid safe-area CSS is INERT in the e2e and only grows on a notched device. Implemented with HAND-WRITTEN author CSS in globals.css (NOT Tailwind arbitrary `pb-[calc(...)]` values — the likely source of the earlier invalid-CSS breakage, since `calc()` requires spaces Tailwind must encode as underscores): `.pb-safe-bottom { padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) }` on the fixed bottom `<nav>` so its tappable row clears the home indicator while its bg still fills to the screen edge; `.pb-bottom-nav { padding-bottom: calc(5rem + env(...)) ; @media(min-width:640px){3rem} }` replacing the (app) layout outer div's `pb-20 sm:pb-12` so content clears the now-taller bar; `html { scroll-padding-bottom }` bumped to `calc(5rem + env(...))` so Playwright/scroll-into-view keeps targets above the bar; and `viewportFit: "cover"` added to the root viewport export so env() is nonzero on real iOS. Every env() term is 0 off iOS → the computed padding is byte-identical to the previous values in the emulator and on desktop. Gate (real 2026-06-24): VERIFY_E2E=1 bash scripts/verify.sh → GREEN in one pass, 931 unit/73 files, 53 e2e (incl. the dashboard bottom-nav clicks and the triage bottom-anchored action/swipe flows that failed before), typecheck/lint/build clean. Measuring the inset first (0px) proved the correct fix is a no-op in tests, so the discipline was to (a) write CSS GUARANTEED valid (author rules, not Tailwind arbitrary-value compilation, which silently emits nothing on a malformed token) and (b) couple the bar height and the content clearance to the SAME env() expression so they can never drift. Invisible on every platform the tests run on, correct on the one they can't — only-change-if-markedly-better applied to a platform-specific polish gap. |
| 91 | R5 | Auto-sync SimpleFIN on page load (reported bug: real transactions "not populating / missing a bunch"). ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed, not assumed): the ONLY path that refreshed real bank data was the manual `syncSimplefinNow()` action (the "Sync now" button) — there was NO automation. `vercel.json` has no `crons` block and git history shows it never did, so `/api/cron/sync` was never scheduled (prod runtime logs: zero hits to it in 7d); and that route syncs via `getProvider()` (demo/Plaid), not `syncFromSimplefin`, so even if scheduled it wouldn't touch SimpleFIN. So nothing pulled new transactions unless the user clicked Sync now. FIX (per the owner's explicit "sync needs to be automatic on every refresh"): a new client `<AutoSync enabled>` mounted once in the (app) layout — on a full page load/refresh (NOT soft client navigations; the layout doesn't remount on those) it calls the real `syncSimplefinNow()` in the background (never blocks render) and `router.refresh()`es the server data only when new rows were ingested **(SUPERSEDED by #316/L.28: it now refreshes whenever the sync reports it CHANGED anything — the ingested-rows predicate silently ignored rewritten balances, due dates and scheduled projections)**. The layout gates it with a cheap indexed `simpleFinConnection` lookup so demo/manual-only users never fire a sync. A 10s `sessionStorage` throttle coalesces rapid reloads / multiple tabs so refresh-spam can't trip the SimpleFIN bridge's rate-limit (which would break syncing — the opposite of the goal). Reverted a half-started Vercel-cron approach (rejected: needs CRON_SECRET + a plan-dependent schedule and only refreshes while the app is CLOSED — on-load was what was asked and has no env/plan deps). Gate (real 2026-06-24): VERIFY_E2E=1 bash scripts/verify.sh → GREEN in one pass, 931 unit/73 files, 53 e2e (demo user has no connection → AutoSync no-op, suite unaffected), typecheck/lint/build clean. HONEST LIMITS: the on-load incremental sync uses start = lastSyncedAt − 5d, so it auto-recovers everything since the last successful sync, but transactions older than each account's original 90-day backfill window are NOT recovered by this (a forced full backfill is a separate follow-up); and the live SimpleFIN network path stays UNVERIFIED in this sandbox — the sync LOGIC is covered by existing tests and the on-load wiring by build + the no-op demo e2e, but whether it pulls the owner's specific missing rows needs the owner to load the site and confirm. | The real defect was structural (manual-only sync), so the right fix makes a sync happen automatically exactly when the user is looking at the app. Client-triggered + non-blocking keeps the page fast (renders current data, then updates on change); refresh-only-on-change avoids needless re-renders; the throttle protects the bank link so the automation can't rate-limit itself into failure. Chose on-load over cron per the explicit request and because it needs no secret/plan and delivers freshness precisely when it's seen. |

Also independently confirmed the real `/link/token/create` endpoint works live (the one call `plaid:validate` never made, since it uses the sandbox public-token bypass). Scoping 'unsafe-eval' to dev keeps production's strict CSP intact while making the dev server actually usable for the manual Link test. |

| 222 | TASKS 2.1 | **Ask conversation frame — deterministic ellipsis resolution.** New pure `src/lib/engine/assistant/frame.ts`: `frameFromIntent(intent)` distils the previous turn's RESOLVED intent into a slot frame `{kind, timeframe, target, merchant, limit}`; `resolveEllipsis(question, today, frame, custom)` rebuilds the same intent with the one slot the fragment names swapped ("what about last month?" / "and groceries?" / "at Costco?"). **Consulted ONLY when `parseAssistantQuery` returns `unknown`**, so a self-sufficient question is never re-interpreted and every pre-existing route is byte-identical with or without a frame. It originates nothing: each slot comes from the already-validated frame or from the user's own words via the parser's OWN helpers (`parseExplicitTimeframe`, `resolveSpendTarget`, `extractMerchantPhrase`) — `parseTimeframe` was split so "names no timeframe" is distinguishable from "says this month", and the merchant tokenizer + the #168 payment-method guard are now shared, never re-implemented. **Session state lives in the answer, not the server:** `AssistantAnswer.intent` is echoed to the client and handed back on the next ask, so there is no table, no session store, and no cross-tab coupling; the returning value is UNTRUSTED and goes through the same `validateIntent` gate the LLM's proposals do before it becomes a frame (a forged frame can only re-ask a question about the caller's own ownership-scoped data). Order is parser → frame → LLM, so a deterministic answer always beats a model call (rule 5). Frame-resolved asks ARE written to the UnknownQuestion ledger but tagged `frame:<kind>`: the phrasing is context-DEPENDENT, so TASKS 2.3 must never mine it into a context-free vocab rule, while a mis-resolution still leaves a trail. Deliberate NON-support: "same for Amex" abstains — #168 established that payment methods are not merchants, and the frame reuses that guard rather than contradicting it. | Audit §3 idea #2 (impact 9): the assistant had amnesia — every follow-up had to restate the whole question. Pure parser state beats a conversational LLM here: it is deterministic, testable, free, and it cannot invent a figure. |
| 223 | TASKS 2.1 | **Frame hostile-critic cycle 1 (fresh-context Fable): FAIL — 3 P1 + 4 P2, all fixed in-cycle.** The P1s were all the same disease — the frame answering a question the user did not ask: (1) a timeframe-FIRST fragment ("and this month at costco?") silently dropped the merchant and answered the carried category; (2) negation was unmodelled, so "restaurants not groceries" answered GROCERIES (synonym order is first-match-wins); (3) the assistant's own vocabulary became merchant probes ("what about income?" → "No spending at Income"), which also STOLE the question from the LLM classifier that routes it correctly. Fixes: merchant search anywhere in the fragment; NEGATION_WORDS abstain (a LEADING "no," stays a correction cue); INTENT_NOUNS + PRONOUNS abstain on the merchant path; QUESTION_WORDS ("why", "should", "vs", "is") abstain the whole fragment before ANY slot extraction (P2-4 — the guard had existed only on the merchant path); `largest_purchases` dropped from SPEND_FAMILY, because "what about at Costco?" after "my biggest purchase" means the biggest purchase AT Costco, which no engine computes — abstain beats silently answering a merchant TOTAL (P2-5); `validateIntent` now bounds month (01–12), label (≤40) and merchant (≤64) — it had never been a client-facing boundary before this slice (P2-6); a CARRIED deictic window is re-labelled against today, since "this month" framed in June is a false name in July, though the window itself never moves (P2-7). Every guard fails SAFE: a false hit abstains to the honest `unknown` and the LLM rescue still gets its turn. Accepted limitations: one-turn memory (an intervening `unknown` clears the frame); no comparison intent exists, so "compared to last month?" answers a lone figure; a novel non-category noun ("what about my raise?") can still read as a merchant and answer "No spending at raise" — exactly what the parser does today for the same word, so the frame introduces no new sin. | The critic earned its keep: all three P1s were confident-wrong money answers that the 29 happy-path tests missed, and each is now locked by a fail-old regression test. |

| 225 | TASKS 2.3 | **Learned vocabulary — the weekly mining loop (audit §4.2 loop 2).** New additive `VocabEntry` (per-user, `@@unique([userId, phrase])`, cascade) + pure `src/lib/engine/vocab/vocab.ts` (`normalizePhrase`, `matchVocab`, `mineVocab`) + Prisma-only `src/server/vocab.ts` + weekly `/api/cron/vocab` (Mon 16:00). **The load-bearing safety property: an entry supplies an intent KIND and nothing else.** Every parameter — timeframe, category, merchant, amount, age — is re-derived from the asker's own words by `intentFromKind` and re-validated by `validateIntent`, which is byte-for-byte the contract the LLM classifier has lived under since #75. The vocab layer is therefore exactly as powerful as the model route it replaces, minus the model call: a wrong entry can route to a wrong KIND, and can never inject a figure, a window, or a category. Routing order is parser → frame → **vocab** → LLM (deterministic beats a model call, rule 5), consulted ONLY on a parser-`unknown`, so every existing route is byte-identical and the demo (which learns nothing, see #226) is untouched. **The key** is the PII-scrubbed question: the scrub already masks digits and amounts, so one key spans "retire at 60" and "retire at 67" — exactly the spans the answer path re-derives. **PER-USER by construction, a deliberate deviation from the audit's "≥N distinct users" clustering:** a phrase is user-authored text that has been scrubbed, not anonymized (names, employers and clinics survive), so pooling it would copy one person's language into another's routing table and onto their screen; the audit's own "/asks" branch is satisfiable per-user, and a wrong global rule has N users' blast radius instead of one. **The ladder:** shadow (minted from ≥3 unanimous INDEPENDENT rescues; not served, accruing held-out evidence) → flagged (≥2 held-out agreements, zero disagreements; served with the same "I interpreted your question" hedge an LLM answer carries) → active (≥2 disclosed serves, no rejection; served, disclosed as learned) → retired (TERMINAL tombstone). **Self-confirmation is structurally impossible:** rows the loop's own entries resolved are tagged `vocab:<kind>` in the UnknownQuestion ledger and count ONLY as `served`, never as evidence, so a bare kind always means an independent resolution; `frame:`-tagged rows (#222) make a phrase permanently ineligible, since a context-free rule for "what about last month?" would be a bug. Every count is recomputed from the ledger each run, never incremented. Undo is first-class and terminal: "Not what I meant" on the answer, "Forget this" on Settings → AI trust, and the miner can never re-mint a retired phrase from the evidence the user just rejected. | Audit §4.2 loop 2: the parser gets smarter every week with zero deploys, and — because the rule is deterministic and free — it keeps working with no LLM key at all, no 7s timeout, and no rate limit. Whole-question keys rather than the audit's n-gram clusters: an n-gram rule can fire on a question it was never mined from, which is precisely the audit's own named failure mode ("promoting a rule that would have mis-routed a later question"), and there is no real ledger data yet to tune a clustering threshold against. Learn the narrow thing that is provably safe now; earn the general one later, on evidence. |
| 226 | TASKS 2.3 | **Vocab hostile-critic cycle 1 (3 fresh-context Fable critics in parallel — routing/money, the learning loop, authz+privacy): FAIL — 0 P0, 5 P1, 11 P2. All P1s and every actionable P2 fixed in-cycle and regression-locked.** **P1-1 (privacy, the worst): the shared demo account learned.** The demo login is credential-free and ONE-CLICK, so every anonymous visitor is the same user row — the miner would have mined one stranger's typed question ("can melissa and i afford ivf at …") and rendered it in the next visitor's /settings, under copy promising it is shared with no one. Fixed: `learningDisabled()` short-circuits mine/serve/list for `DEMO_USER_ID`, which moved to a NextAuth-free `src/lib/demo-user.ts` so the cron import graph stays clean (#220); the household feature had already fenced the demo user off for the same reason (#210), and this is now the second instance of the rule *anything that accumulates a user's own INPUT and shows it back must opt the demo user out*. **P1-2: `VocabEntry` was an undisclosed store** — PRIVACY.md now describes it and lists it in the deletion cascade. **P1-3: the miner could clobber a tombstone.** It reads, decides, then writes; a "Forget this" landing inside that window was overwritten by the stale decision — and since the rejection lives nowhere else, it was gone for good, the entry resumed serving, and it self-promoted. Fixed with `status: { not: 'retired' }` in the write filter: a tombstone always wins the race. **P1-4: the loop went blind at the exact moment it started affecting answers.** A served entry short-circuits the LLM, so no independent row about that phrase could ever be written again — held-out evidence froze, flagged→active promoted on the entry's OWN serves, and the "one disagreement retires it" rule was unreachable. That fails audit constitution (d)+(e) outright. Fixed with `auditServableEntries()`: once a week, off the answer path, every SERVED phrase is replayed against the classifier that never sees the rule, and a disagreement retires it. Fails safe both ways — no key or any error means no opinion and no change, and a FALSE retire costs the user nothing (the question simply returns to the route it had before it was ever learned), which is why one disagreement is enough. **P1-5 (pre-existing, in the parser): "how much did I spend at 星巴克 last month" answered the ALL-SPENDING TOTAL, undisclosed** — both #166 abstain guards are ASCII-only, so a store named in a non-Latin script tokenized to nothing ("at 星巴克" → the total) or was silently mangled ("with Zürich Café" → merchant "zrich"). A true figure under a false question: the cardinal sin, in a file this slice touches. Now abstains before the tokenizer sees it. **P2s fixed:** the learned kind must ROUND-TRIP (`[num]` masking collapses "pay off my car by 2027" and "…by 65" into one key, and `intentFromKind` silently degrades `debt_free_by_date` → `debt_payoff` when no date parses — so a rule mined from the date form was answering the age form with a different question; it now abstains); `normalizePhrase` refuses any non-ASCII key (normalization would DELETE it, collapsing questions that name different people into one rule); the held-out boundary is now DATA-derived (`evidenceThrough` = the newest supporting row) instead of the miner's wall clock, which clock skew could otherwise turn into self-validation; `MAX_ENTRIES_PER_USER = 200` caps the routing table; the mint `catch` no longer swallows anything but P2002; the e2e fixture refuses to run outside the throwaway e2e database. **ACCEPTED, not fixed:** `status` is a durable ratchet — an entry whose supporting rows age out of the 2000-row mining window keeps serving with recomputed-to-zero counts. Deliberate (a rule that passed its gates should not be un-learned because the ledger scrolled), and safe because every DOWNWARD path stays open forever on no evidence budget at all: user rejection, held-out disagreement, a `frame:` row, and the weekly independent re-check can each retire a serving entry at any time. | Three parallel critics with different lenses was the right call: the routing critic proved the kind-only claim held, and then the OTHER two found what it could not see — that the loop's back half (undo durability, post-flag monitoring, demo privacy) was where the design actually leaked. Every P1 was invisible from inside the feature's own happy path, and two came with failing repros. |

P3s: `maxDuration = 300` on the one cron that makes outbound calls. ACCEPTED, not fixed: an audit-retire is TERMINAL like a user's rejection, so one stochastic misclassification permanently forecloses a phrase — the cost is that the question returns to the LLM route it had before it was ever learned (zero user-visible harm), and the asymmetry against a false PROMOTE (a true figure under a false question) justifies the bias; it is now at least visible in the audit trail rather than silent. Two lessons, both now in the ledger: a guard must walk the same input as the thing it guards, and a safety abstention that widens beyond its target is a regression wearing a safety jacket. |

## #338 (O.14a): a fault on our side may not be reported as a wrong password — and the stale brand host still served the app

**The copy defect, fixed.** `signInWithPassword` caught `AuthError` and returned "Invalid email or
password." for every member of that taxonomy. `CallbackRouteError` is in it, and that is what Auth.js
raises when `authorize()` itself throws — the `prisma.user.findUnique` inside it can fail on a cold or
flaky connection. So an outage on our side made a CLAIM about what the reader typed, and it was false; it
also spent one of his eight per-account failed-attempt credits on an attempt he never failed. Fixed by
naming the infrastructure types explicitly.

**The direction of that list is the decision.** An UNRECOGNISED `AuthError` deliberately stays on the
credential path — keeps the "invalid" sentence AND keeps consuming the throttle budget — because excusing
unknown errors hands an attacker who can provoke any unusual AuthError a way to opt out of brute-force
throttling. Being wrong in the excused direction costs a confusing sentence; being wrong in the other
direction costs the throttle. Locked both ways (`rate-limit-durable.test.ts`), mutation-proven.

**Why the cause of the owner's intermittent failure is NOT claimed here.** Four candidate mechanisms were
killed rather than shipped: `MissingCSRF` is impossible (`next-auth/lib/actions.js` passes
`skipCSRFCheck`), verification is deterministic (scrypt, per-password salt, no pepper/env/clock), the
pre-hydration controlled-input class does not apply (the inputs are uncontrolled by deliberate design),
and the reveal toggle's capture-phase `type` flip loses no value in chromium or WebKit (measured, 3 cases
each — and Playwright WebKit is explicitly not his iOS Safari). A PII-free discriminator now records
`reason=no-user | bad-hash` so the next occurrence names its own cause; the reader's copy is identical
either way, so it cannot become an account-enumeration oracle.

**Separately, and NOT claimed as the cause:** `pulse-finance-mu.vercel.app` — the app's pre-rename brand
host — was still serving the full live application at 200, as was `aimplifi-reiforge.vercel.app`, while
only `aimplifi.app` redirected to `www.aimplifi.app` (measured with curl against production). A renamed
personal-finance app answering on its old origin is worth closing on its own terms: a password manager
keys credentials per origin, so a second live host is a second place a stale credential can live, and
sessions there are separate from the canonical host's.

Fixed at the PLATFORM layer (`vercel.json` `redirects` with a `host` condition), not in middleware,
because the middleware matcher deliberately excludes `/sign-in` — the very page this matters on — and
widening that regex to carry a host redirect would put a security-load-bearing pattern at risk for an
unrelated reason.

**Deliberate residual:** `aimplifi-reiforge.vercel.app` and the per-deployment `aimplifi-<hash>.vercel.app`
URLs are left serving, because they are the instruments the repo uses to verify a deployment reached
production (L.23) and to exercise previews; redirecting them would blind the deploy check. Only the stale
BRAND host is redirected.

## #339 (O.13a critic cycle 1): a typed key is a PATTERN, and every guard the app has was written for an identity

Two fresh-context critics, different lenses (money/data-integrity; claims/privacy), both **FAIL**, converging
independently on the demo fence and on the preview promising rows the pipeline refuses. 2 P0 + 7 P1, all
fixed and locked. The unifying finding is one sentence: **every existing safeguard assumed a rule's key was
an exact identity the reader attached to one payee, and a keyword is a substring that generalises to rows he
has never seen.**

That is why the sign guard mattered most. `cardone -> income` is obviously right for the deposits he was
looking at, and obviously wrong for the management fee that arrives next month — and filing an outflow into
an Income category does not merely mis-label it, it DELETES it: `isSpendRow` drops Income-group rows, so the
spending disappears from reports, trends and budgets while `monthlyFlows` still counts it as an expense.
Two surfaces, one row, disagreeing by the amount, with no badge and no review. The guard now applies to typed
rules — and the FIRST fix was itself wrong, because reusing `learnedSignOk` also refused a positive row in a
spend category, which is the documented refund convention. The guard is asymmetric on purpose, and the
slice's own lock caught the over-correction within minutes.

The second P0 is the same mistake in the write path: the apply set was every row the user owns. A split
CHILD carries its parent's descriptor, so a keyword rule collapsed an allocation the reader had made by
hand — the only record that it existed — and it also re-filed a detected transfer, cleared a review pin no
undo can restore, and touched investment and non-USD rows no register page renders. All five exclusions
already existed in three sibling writers; this one was authored from the engine's perspective (which rows
match) instead of the product's (which rows are the app's to decide).

**The claims half was worse than the code half, and that is the transferable part.** Three strings told the
reader an empty rule "would match everything" — the RATIONALE for the guard, shipped as a fact, when the
engine does the exact opposite and says so in capitals. The builder told him to check his spelling against
"the original bank text" that the register does not display; and this same session's brand work widened that
gap, because `MACYS LENOX SQUARE` now displays as `Macy's`, which never matches as typed (4 of 6 executed
cases failed). Two changes shipped hours apart worked against each other, and neither author noticed —
mitigated now by showing his real descriptors when a key matches nothing, with the row-level fix carried to
O.13b.

**Process notes worth keeping.** Parallel critics with different lenses found the same two defects
independently, which is the strongest available signal a finding is real; each also found P1s the other
missed. The `undoCorrections` finding is a reminder that a capability with one caller is barely a capability:
it had existed for months and the rewrite of months of history had no way back. And the stale-list defect was
invisible to every unit test and to a passing e2e — it only surfaced because the spec asserted the row
appears WITHOUT a reload.


## #340 (O.13c + critic cycle 1): Simplifi-parity rules — and the discovery that giving an existing column a new meaning is a data migration nobody wrote

**What shipped.** Four Simplifi-parity additions to the typed keyword rules from O.13a: a
**Rename Payee** action, **OR keyword groups**, the **account + amount conditions** the
`CategorizationRule` table has carried unexposed since Phase 2, and **edit-in-place** (O.13a
offered only delete-and-retype, which silently dropped the rule's undo lineage).

**The rename was built as an IDENTITY, not a label — and that deviates from the plan in
TASKS deliberately.** The queued design was an additive `Merchant.displayName` plus "one
resolver at the UI boundary", with the stated risk that *"every surface that prints a merchant
name must read the same resolver, or two pages will disagree about what the same payee is
called."* That risk is real and this build sidesteps it entirely: a rename re-points the row's
`merchantId` at a `Merchant` whose canonical IS the name the reader typed. Every surface that
already reads `merchant.canonical` — register, merchant lens, recurring — shows the new name
with **zero** new resolver and no possibility of two pages disagreeing. `rawDescriptor` is
never touched, so the bank's text stays the permanent record and the match key. The cost is
that renaming is a write over history rather than a view-time transform, which is why it is
gated behind the same explicit apply-to-existing checkbox the category refile uses.

**The OR groups were the expensive lesson, and both fresh-context critics found it
independently — the strongest available signal a finding is real.** The first cut encoded the
groups into the EXISTING `matchKeywords` column, using `|` as the divider, and taught
`parseKeywords` to treat `|` as a separator. Every docblock called the encoding "lossless BY
CONSTRUCTION", and for values the new codec wrote itself, it was. The claim was answering the
wrong question. `|` was an **ordinary character inside a keyword** under the parser that wrote
every row already in the database, so the change silently redefined stored data: an AND key
that required the literal `us|y47` became an OR that fires on `y47` alone, at 9900 bps with
`needsReview: false`, no badge and no review. The tail is worse — `shell|a` passed O.13a's
length floor as one 7-character token, and would have decoded to the group `["a"]`, which
matches nearly every descriptor and mass-files an entire account into one category. Two
docblocks and the schema comment asserted this could not happen ("a pre-O.13c row has no
`|`"); the assertion was simply false, and a test titled *"every pre-O.13c key decodes as
before"* exercised only a key with no `|` — a tautology under both codecs.

**The fix is structural, not a patch: the new encoding got its own column.**
`matchKeywordGroups` is additive and nullable, written only by the O.13c codec, authoritative
when present. `matchKeywords` keeps the pure-AND meaning it has always had, is read by a
decoder that keeps the pre-O.13c separators **forever**, and still carries a multi-group rule's
FIRST group — so the column stays a truthful key for every row, remains the "is this a typed
rule" discriminator, and if the group column were ever lost the rule degrades to one group:
**narrower, never wider.** The per-group length floor is now re-applied on the READ path too,
in the one shared `storedKeywordGroups` basis that both the engine loader and the rules list
decode through, so the page can never render a key the engine does not execute. The
transferable rule: **a stored value's meaning may never change under it, and a guard that runs
only at creation is advisory.** `server/rules.ts` already re-applied `isAggregateCanonical` at
load time with the comment *"defense in depth … even if a rule row predates the creation-time
guard"* — the identical argument, one function away, not applied.

**Two more P1s, both from reasoning about a field by only one of its jobs.** (1) The shared
apply-to-history writer claimed undo lineage unconditionally, so editing a rule, re-applying,
and clicking the toast's Undo **deleted the rule the reader had only meant to edit** — while
the builder's optimistic list kept rendering it, so there was no signal at all. Lineage is now
claimed on the create path only. (2) The rename was applied to rows the sign guard had
**refused** to file, on the stated premise that "a rename is a display identity, not a filing,
so no money moves." That premise ignores `merchantId`'s second job: it is the batch key
`similarTransactionsWhere` uses, and `recategorize({scope:'merchant'})` re-files already-filed
rows in that batch. So the rename built a mixed-sign merchant group in which one later "file
all similar" would turn three real deposits into spend — the exact erasure the sign guard
exists to prevent, reached by a different door. The rename set now takes the same
`signWouldErase` filter the refile does, which also settles a contradiction between the two
rename paths: `categorize` renames only a rule that actually FILED, so before this the same row
would have been named one way by backfill and another by the next sync.

**A fix that broke the thing it measured, caught by its own lock.** Making the "N payees
renamed" count truthful meant excluding rows already carrying the name, written as
`NOT: { merchantId: merchant.id }`. In SQL's three-valued logic that is UNKNOWN for a NULL
column, so every unnamed row — the majority, and the entire point of a rename — was silently
excluded and every rename reported 0 and wrote nothing. The lock written for the count claim
caught it the same minute. Predicate is now an explicit `OR: [{ merchantId: null }, …]`.

**Recorded residuals, deliberate and documented rather than fixed:** clearing the rename field
does not put the bank's text back on rows already renamed (it can only be overwritten with
another name); `runBackfillForUser` honors a rule's category action but not its rename, so a
rule created without apply-to-existing leaves its rows under two payee identities; a rename
whose text differs only in case from an existing canonical (`costco` vs `Costco`) mints a
second `Merchant` row that looks identical in the register, because a portable
case-insensitive lookup is not available across SQLite and Postgres in Prisma; and rules still
require a category, so a rename-only rule is not expressible.

## #341 (O.15 slice 1): nothing the app claims is a dead end — and a link is refused where it would land on someone else's rows

Owner's verdict, 2026-07-30: *"no cohesion in the app… most def not at parity with
Mint/Simplifi."* The concrete defect underneath the word "cohesion" was that surfaces
named a merchant and stopped there. `/recurring` stated "you pay X $15.99/mo" and the
name did nothing; the Today feed asserted a charge was "larger than the typical $11.56
there" and offered exactly one control — Dismiss. The app made claims about named
merchants and gave the reader no way to check any of them.

**The rule:** a named merchant is a way in to the rows behind the claim. Implemented as
one builder, `merchantRegisterHref()`, added beside `categoryRegisterHref` in
`src/lib/engine/transactions/links.ts` — the module that already declared itself the one
author of every drill-down href while two inline `?merchant=` template literals lived
outside it (`transaction-list.tsx`, `transaction-detail-view.tsx`). Both are migrated onto
it. A first draft of this entry said "four migrated" and a critic checked the actual
commit: the other two edited call sites (`coach/page.tsx`, `life-energy-card.tsx`) were
plain `<span>`s that became NEW links in this same slice — they were never migrations, and
describing them as such would have sent a reviewer past two of the sites carrying the P0
below.

**Why the merchant builder returns `string` and the category builder returns `string |
null`.** They are not inconsistent; they are fenced against different holes. A category
link is hung on a FIGURE, so `CategoryFigure` makes `from`/`to` required — a window-less
category link lands on all-history, a larger total than any figure that could have been
clicked — and it refuses ids the register's `<select>` cannot DISPLAY, because landing on
correctly-filtered rows under a control reading "All categories" is still wrong. A
merchant link is hung on a NAME. "Netflix" is not an amount, so there is no sum for the
destination to disagree with and no window to carry; and the register's merchant filter
is free text, which displays whatever it is handed, so there is no rows-right/control-
wrong hole to fence.

**The destination holds by construction, and that was checked rather than assumed.** The
register computes `merchantName` as `t.merchant?.canonical ?? normalizeMerchant(
t.rawDescriptor).canonical` (server/transactions.ts:262) and matches it EXACTLY,
case-insensitively (`query.ts:200` — there is no substring fallback to soften a mangled
parameter). `RecurringSeries.merchantCanonical` is resolved against `Merchant.canonical`
(server/recurring.ts:195–199), which is the same string. Aggregate pseudo-merchants
("ATM Withdrawal", "Zelle Payment") therefore link honestly to the register's own
grouping of those rows rather than to nothing.

**`encodeURIComponent`, not `URLSearchParams`, and it is not a style choice.** Under an
exact-equality filter a mangled escape does not degrade the destination, it EMPTIES it —
and an empty register is not an error, it is a page reading "no transactions" about a
charge the reader is looking straight at, returning HTTP 200 and logging nothing.
`URLSearchParams.toString()` emits a space as `+`, which is only a space to a parser
applying form-encoding rules. The four migrated call sites already emitted `%20`, so
keeping that byte-for-byte is what makes the refactor provably behaviour-preserving
rather than probably behaviour-preserving.

**Two deliberate refusals, both recorded at the call site rather than left to look like
oversights:**

1. **The household shared list keeps plain text.** Every other merchant name in the app
   names a row the reader OWNS. Those rows belong to a PARTNER, and the register is
   viewer-scoped (`getTransactions(session.user.id, …)`) while its household section
   comes from `getSharedTransactionsView()`, which takes no filter at all and so cannot
   narrow to a merchant even in principle. A link would land the reader on their OWN
   charges at that name — a different set, silently — or, where they have none, on an
   empty register reading as "there are no charges here" about a charge they can see.
   Same answer as `categoryRegisterHref`'s null: refuse rather than assert.
2. **The category label on a `/recurring` row is not linked.** A recurring series is a
   cadence, not a sum, so it has no month window to hand `CategoryFigure`. The honest
   link on that row is the merchant, which asserts no figure at all.

**The Today feed gets a separate affordance, not a linkified substring.** `detail` is a
money SENTENCE assembled in `today-feed-copy.ts` whose every clause is audited copy
(estimate disclosures, no-shame framing, the runway formula). Splitting it into React
nodes at each of its four kinds would mean changing money copy to add a link. `merchant`
is already a first-class field on the proposal, so the row points at the register without
touching a word of what it says — and the link is gated on that field being non-null,
because the copy itself falls back to "this source" and a link reading "View charges at
this source" would filter by nothing.

**Locks.** `tests/unit/merchant-register-links.test.ts` round-trips eight hostile real-
world merchant names (`&`, `#`, `+`, `%`, `=`, a curly apostrophe, non-ASCII) through a
REAL `new URL()` parse rather than `href.split('?')[1]` — measured: the split version
keeps 6 of 8 green on a builder that does no escaping at all, because a manual split
never lets `#` start a fragment. `tests/e2e/no-dead-ends.spec.ts` walks the routes and
reads the DOM, because a unit test on a builder cannot see whether the string is on the
page (the O.13b inert-banner lesson). Both were mutation-proven: swapping the two new
links for plain `<span>`s and rebuilding fails exactly 3 of the 6 e2e tests and leaves
the other 3 green.

### O.15 slice 1 — critic cycle 1 (two fresh-context critics, both FAIL, and they did not overlap)

**The P0 neither the unit lock nor the e2e could have caught, because both were built
out of the same string.** `merchant-register-links.test.ts` constructs its fixture rows
with the very name it hands the builder (`view(id, merchantName)`), so it can only ever
prove the URL round-trips — never that the app puts the RIGHT name into it. The e2e runs
on a demo seed with zero divergence. The critic executed a probe and landed the reader on
**0 of 4 rows**.

There are TWO merchant name-spaces here:

* the register displays and matches the STORED name, `t.merchant?.canonical ??
  normalizeMerchant(t.rawDescriptor).canonical` (server/transactions.ts:262, query.ts:200,
  exact and case-insensitive);
* `/recurring`, the Today feed's unusual-charge row and `/coach` display a LIVE
  RE-DERIVATION, `normalizeMerchant(rawDescriptor).canonical` — `RecurringTxn` carries no
  merchant relation at all (recurring/detect.ts:187, anomaly/detect.ts:101,
  server/coach.ts:239).

They agree until something changes the stored name without touching the descriptor, and
O.13c's rename-payee rule does exactly that: it upserts a `Merchant` with `canonical:
renameTo` and re-points `Transaction.merchantId`, leaving `rawDescriptor` alone forever
(server/keyword-rules.ts:598–621). After a rename the register says "Netflix (family
plan)" while `/recurring` still says "Netflix", so a link built from the `/recurring` name
matches nothing.

**Decision: ship the links, pin the divergence, and queue the identity fix — with the
reasoning written down so it can be falsified.**

1. *It is older than the links.* The Merchant Lens already joins these two name-spaces
   and already fails the same way (server/transactions.ts:334 compares
   `s.merchantCanonical` against the register's `profile.merchant`). `/recurring` was
   ALREADY displaying the pre-rename name as plain text. The links did not create the
   split; they made it reachable in one tap.
2. *Failure direction, counted honestly.* Leaving plain text is a dead end for 100% of
   names and every reader. Shipping is a working link for every name that has not been
   renamed and a dead end only for those that have. Shipping is strictly better in
   expectation, and the harm is a visibly empty list rather than a wrong money figure —
   this is a browse-and-audit surface, not an instruction.
3. *The real fix is not available cheaply and must not be faked.* Unifying the
   name-spaces means threading merchant identity through the shared snapshot into
   `detectRecurring` — which changes what a recurring series is KEYED by, and so touches
   detection, price-change history, income-pause identity and the scheduled projection.
   That is engine work at the tier this repo reserves for it. The tempting shortcut —
   widening the register's filter to also match the normalized descriptor — was rejected:
   it papers over an identity defect by making a filter fuzzy, and it silently widens the
   Merchant Lens's money figures, which are computed from the filtered rows.
4. *So it is PINNED, not described.* `merchant-register-links.test.ts` now asserts the
   broken behaviour under a rename fixture with an explicit instruction that a failure
   means the bug is FIXED and the test should be deleted. A divergence you cannot close
   gets a test that explains itself, so closing it means changing something that argues
   back.

**The other findings, all real, all fixed in this cycle:**

* A `toContain` assertion whose own comment claimed it would catch "Barnes & Noble"
  truncating to "Barnes" — and which that truncation PASSES, because a substring check can
  never catch truncation. Now `toBe`.
* `MERCHANT_LINK_CLASS` shipped `hover:underline` only, reproducing verbatim the 380px
  defect this module already recorded for category figures: on a phone there is no hover,
  so the affordance did not exist. It now carries a resting dotted underline matching
  `CATEGORY_LINK_CLASS` — one inspectable idiom across the app, which is the cohesion the
  owner asked for. Locked.
* Its docblock claimed to stop drift while four merchant links in the same commit carried
  hand-written class strings and no focus ring. Now applied everywhere except the detail
  view's footer nav link, which matches its "Back to transactions" neighbour on purpose —
  and the docblock names that exception instead of claiming universality.
* The builder's justification for never returning null claimed "the register's merchant
  filter is a free-text box that displays whatever it is given". There is no such control:
  `transaction-filters.tsx` renders Type/Account/Category/From/To only. The name is echoed
  only by a lens that ABSTAINS on thin history — i.e. it is least visible exactly where the
  destination looks emptiest. Recorded as a real weakness with a queued UI fix, not
  dressed up: unlike a category id there is no predicate a builder could evaluate, since
  every merchant name is equally displayable and equally unshown.
* "View charges at X" rendered on `income_pause` rows, calling a paycheck a charge one
  line under copy audited to say the opposite. Now kind-aware ("View deposits from").
* `truncate` on flex children whose parents lacked `min-w-0` — the exact rule this
  slice's own docblock states, violated in two of the files it was written for.

**Still open, recorded rather than smoothed over:** `detectRecurring` has no
`isAggregateCanonical` guard where `anomaly/detect.ts:102` and `income/pause.ts:196` both
do, so a rent-by-Zelle series renders as "Zelle Payment" and now links to a register
mixing every unrelated Zelle payee. And the feed's opportunity kinds hard-set
`merchant: null` (select.ts:218) although `Opportunity.merchant` exists, so "A
subscription's price went up" still names nobody — the most anonymous claim in the app,
untouched by a slice titled "nothing the app claims is a dead end".
